The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a robust median combination may offer further robustness.
test a weighted combination using inverse_error weights to see if explicit error weighting beats robust trimmed mean on this trend‑dominated, ranking‑unstable series.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a simple mean may be a useful baseline to compare robustness.
I will test a DBA combination on the full pool to see if a more sophisticated optimization can beat the mean, given the unstable ranking and trend‑dominated regime.
Test a weighted combination on the reduced, low‑error pool (trend‑dominated, unstable ranking) to see if a more focused inverse‑error weighting improves over the mean.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a robust median over a small, diverse pool may improve robustness.
test a per‑horizon “best‑per‑horizon” weighting on the full pool to capture potential horizon‑dependent winners in this trend‑dominated series.
Test a weighted combination on the diverse pool4 with softmax_neg_error to see if a more aggressive weighting on the best pool improves over mean.
The ranking is unstable and we have a small, diverse pool (pool5) from forward selection. Testing a weighted combo with inverse error on this subset may improve robustness.
Test a simple mean over the diverse pool4 to see if reducing model count improves robustness in a trend‑dominated series with unstable ranking.

decision.justification: Selected 'mean on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9951. Series context: trend strength 0.6776 and seasonal strength 0.29; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.053); 4 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 1.59.
